name: SplitSection
title: SplitSection
summary: Two-column section with a photo on one side and eyebrow, headline, lead and actions on the other; image-left/text-right by default, reversible.
whenToUse: Use for "About ISM", programme introductions (dot.Bible app, HD Radio, ISM Publishing) and any section that pairs one strong photo with a short story.
Alternate `.dp-split` and `.dp-split-rev` down a page so photos zigzag.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for more than one paragraph of copy or for lists of items; use NumberedList or Card grids.
Do not use without a real photo; use PageIntro or CenteredCta instead.

props.name: imageSrc
props.description: Photo URL. Use a real ISM photo of people reading or listening.

props.name: imageAlt
props.description: Alt text saying what the photo shows. Use "" only if purely decorative.

props.name: reverse
props.description: Put the photo on the right (text left). The photo stays first in the DOM so mobile stacks image-then-text.

props.name: title
props.description: Headline, rendered as `<h2>`. At most about 10 words; wrap one word in `<span className="em">`.

props.name: actions
props.description: At most two actions: a secondary and a ghost `Button`.

props.name: headingId
props.description: Id of the h2; generated when omitted.

variantNotes: Media is 4:5 on desktop and 4:3 on mobile, with the `.media` 20px radius.
Columns are equal with a 64px (`--space-8`) gap, vertically centred. Under 768px it stacks: photo first, then text, 32px gap.
On a light page, wrap it in a white card (`--radius-lg`, `--gray-200` border, 48px padding) or leave it on `--off-white`; on `.sec-ink` the type switches to its dark styles.

states.universal: See rules/states.md for the seven required states and their hooks.

rules: Actions: at most two. Use `.btn-secondary` + `.btn-ghost`; use `.btn-primary` only if this section holds the page's main action, and then only one.
↗ on a link means it goes to another page.
Headline at most about 10 words; lead one or two sentences.
Use a real ISM photo of people reading or listening, never an illustration or screenshot here.
Keep the photo first in the DOM in both variants so mobile always stacks image-then-text.

accessibility: Use a real heading (`h2`) and label the section with `aria-labelledby`.
Write alt text that says what the photo shows; use `alt=""` only if it is purely decorative.
Reversing with `order` keeps reading order sensible because the photo carries no essential text.
